review.tagline: PyTorch training framework that removes loop, device and distributed boilerplate
review.summary: PyTorch Lightning wraps PyTorch models in a LightningModule and a Trainer that handles the training loop, mixed precision, checkpointing, logging and multi-device scaling. The same package ships Lightning Fabric, a lower-level API that keeps your own loop and adds device placement and distributed strategies (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed). Runs on CPU, CUDA, Apple Silicon (MPS) and TPU.
review.audience: ML engineers training or finetuning PyTorch models across GPUs or nodes
strengths: Same code scales from CPU to multi-node GPU or TPU by changing Trainer arguments
Fabric offers a minimal-diff path for existing PyTorch loops, with DDP, FSDP and DeepSpeed
Built-in early stopping and checkpointing callbacks; loggers for TensorBoard, W&B, Comet, MLflow
Exports to TorchScript and ONNX; README cites about 300 ms per epoch overhead
weaknesses: Training only; serving needs the separate LitServe project
Trainer requires restructuring code into LightningModule hooks
README promotes Lightning Cloud, and most examples run as Lightning Studios
Abstraction layer over PyTorch can complicate debugging unusual loops
needs: Models: PyTorch nn.Module, TorchScript export, ONNX export
